title: Free AI game maker: a game to play from a few words · {name}
description: Describe a game and get one that plays right in your browser: an original game for a lesson, a party or a rainy day, tested before you see it. Free.
h1: Describe a game, and play it right here.
lede: Give {name} a theme, a lesson to practise or who will play. It designs an original game, builds it, plays it itself to find what breaks, then hands you one that works: with keys, a touch screen or a gamepad, on any device, offline.
cta: Try it with a sample game
try.ask: Make a game for my class of 8-year-olds to practise the 7 times table: answers fall from a tree, and they catch the right one in a basket. Ten sums a round, and gentle when they get one wrong.

made.name: Seven Apples
made.card: Seven Apples. You hold a basket under an apple tree, and you must catch the right answers. The verb: slide the basket under the apple that answers the sum; each catch rings a note higher. The loop: a sum of the 7 times table, three apples falling, one of them right; ten sums a round. The curve: the first four sums can’t be lost; then a wrong apple costs one of three hearts, and apples fall a little faster every three right answers. Controls: left and right move the basket. Look and sound: a night-blue orchard, red apples, a yellow basket; a rising note, a low note, a chord to win.

exact.title: Played before you play it.
exact.why: A game that freezes on its first screen is no game. {name} plays each one out of sight and tells the AI what broke, what each control did and how far it got, before you see it.
exact.cards: Every game is started twice, then each of its controls is held in turn. What broke goes back to the AI, with the line it broke at.
Ask for a game you know and you get an original game of its kind, with its own name, characters and look: never that game drawn again.
In a child’s profile: nothing frightening, no betting, no shop, no daily streak, no timer that punishes. For everyone: no ads and no links out.
where.title: Where your game lives.
where.why: On your device. It plays offline, and reaches nothing on the internet.
where.cards: Your game is one file in your browser, encrypted. Nothing we can read reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and what you attach go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
A game runs in a sealed frame: it loads nothing from the internet and sends nothing to it, whatever its code says.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. Without a sign-up, only the AI on this computer answers.
Everything is drawn and sounded from code: shapes, pixel art, simple sounds. No photos, no recorded music and no voices, unless a picture is yours.
One player, one screen, rounds of a minute or three: a small game, not a studio’s.
No online play and no scores shared between players: what a game saves stays on the device it is played on.
{name} can be wrong. Play a round yourself before you hand it to a class.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Do I need to know how to code?
No. You describe the game, and change it the same way: “make it faster”, “add a level”, “use my class’s vocabulary”.
Can it copy a game I know?
No, and on purpose. You get an original game of the same kind, with its own name, characters and look.
Does it work on a phone or a tablet?
Yes. On a touch screen the game gets buttons for its actions, and it fills the screen when you ask. A gamepad works too.
Yes. Save it as a page that plays in any browser, offline, or publish it at an address of its own.
Does it work in my language?
Yes: every word a player reads is in yours, right to left too, with numbers as your language writes them.
